main.title: The Tomorrow Children
main.subtitle: A town has to be built from a vanished world
main.summary: The Tomorrow Children is Q-Games' PlayStation 4 social adventure, first made available through its Founder's Pack on 6 September 2016 before a full release in October. Projection clones enter the Void to gather the materials needed to rebuild human communities. The player travels between a town and strange islands, collecting resources and returning them for shared construction. Its visual world resembles a distorted collective future, with work and infrastructure giving the adventure its daily rhythm. Progress is visible in the settlement that the gathered materials allow everyone to extend.

cards.heading: A town has to be built from a vanished world
cards.text: The Tomorrow Children is Q-Games' PlayStation 4 social adventure, first made available through its Founder's Pack on 6 September 2016 before a full release in October. Projection clones enter the Void to gather the materials needed to rebuild human communities. The player travels between a town and strange islands, collecting resources and returning them for shared construction. Its visual world resembles a distorted collective future, with work and infrastructure giving the adventure its daily rhythm. Progress is visible in the settlement that the gathered materials allow everyone to extend.

cards.heading: Resources have to reach the people who can use them
cards.text: Wood, metal, coal and crystals supply buildings and utilities, while recovered matryoshka dolls contribute to restoring citizens. Buses connect islands to the town, making transport part of the work rather than an invisible transfer between menus. Tools reshape the landscape and reach resources, but enormous Izverg creatures also threaten the settlement. Gathering and defence therefore depend on one another. The player can be useful by bringing back a necessary material or by helping protect what has already been built, with the town providing the common purpose that connects those different activities.

cards.heading: A shared world closes and finds a second life
cards.text: Dylan Cuthbert directed the game, with music by Joel Corelitz. Sony shut down the original service in 2017, ending the first version's short life. Q-Games later acquired the property and released Phoenix Edition in September 2022, introducing changes that included solo play with computer-controlled companions. The revival demonstrates how strongly the design depended on access to its shared world. Its defining idea remains the visible connection between an individual's apparently modest task and the collective settlement: a small delivery matters because it becomes part of something everyone inhabits.

main.title: Persona 5
main.subtitle: Behind the mask, another life
main.summary: Persona 5 is a 2016 role-playing video game developed by P-Studio.

cards.heading: Persona 5 and the expanded Royal edition
cards.text: Persona 5 is a 2016 role-playing video game developed by P-Studio. The game is the sixth installment in the Persona series, itself a spin-off from the Megami Tensei franchise. Published by Atlus in Japan and North America, and Deep Silver in PAL territories, it was released for PlayStation 3 and PlayStation 4 in Japan on September 15, 2016 and worldwide on April 4, 2017. An enhanced version featuring new content, Persona 5 Royal, was released by Atlus for PlayStation 4 in Japan on October 31, 2019, while parent company Sega published the game worldwide on March 31, 2020. Royal was released on the PlayStation 5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch, and Windows on October 21, 2022.

cards.heading: The Phantom Thieves and a double life
cards.text: As with previous games in the series, the party battles enemies known as Shadows using physical manifestations of their psyche known as Personas. The game incorporates role-playing and dungeon crawling elements alongside social simulation scenarios. Set in modern-day Tokyo, the story follows a player-named high school student, referred to by his codename Joker. After being framed for assault and put on probation, the protagonist relocates to the fictional neighborhood Yongen-Jaya and transfers to a new school. Over the course of a school year, he and other acquainted students awaken to a special power, becoming a group of secret vigilantes referred to as the Phantom Thieves of Hearts. The group explores a supernatural realm born from humanity's subconscious desires nicknamed the Metaverse, in order to steal malevolent intent from the hearts of adults. Its themes revolve around attaining freedom from the limitations of modern society; the story was strongly inspired by picaresque fiction, and the party's Personas were based on literary outlaws and rebels.

cards.heading: A returning creative team at P-Studio
cards.text: First announced in 2013, Persona 5 was developed by P-Studio, an internal development division within Atlus, at the time led by game director and producer Katsura Hashino. Along with Hashino, returning staff from earlier Persona games included character designer Shigenori Soejima and music composer Shoji Meguro. Work on the game began during Persona 4's development and commenced into full production after the release of Catherine in 2011. Initially slated for a late 2014 release date, Persona 5 saw several delays due to being unfinished.

cards.heading: Acclaim, adaptations and a sequel
cards.text: Persona 5 received critical acclaim, with praise directed towards its visual presentation, gameplay, story, characters, and music. The release of Royal saw additional acclaim for its new content and expansion on the original game. Including Royal, Persona 5 is the best-selling title in the Megami Tensei franchise, with over 11.8 million copies sold by June 2026. Since its release, critics have regarded Persona 5 as one of the greatest video games of all time. As with prior series entries, related media based on the game have been produced, including four spin-off games, manga and anime adaptations, and the cast's appearances in other games—most notably Joker's appearance in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate (2018). A sequel, Persona 5 Strikers, was released on February 20, 2020, developed by Koei Tecmo's Omega Force studio in collaboration with Atlus.

main.title: Forza Horizon 3
main.subtitle: A festival on the roads of Australia
main.summary: Forza Horizon 3 is a 2016 racing game developed by Playground Games and published by Microsoft Studios for the Xbox One and Windows.

cards.heading: Running the Horizon festival in Australia
cards.text: Forza Horizon 3 is a 2016 racing game developed by Playground Games and published by Microsoft Studios for the Xbox One and Windows. It is the ninth instalment in the Forza series and the third instalment in the Forza Horizon sub-series. The game is set in a fictionalised Australia, where the player is the leader of the titular Horizon car festival and has to expand the festival by completing events to earn fans. Like previous Forza Horizon games, it features an open world environment where players can freely roam the map.

cards.heading: Playground researches Australia's varied regions
cards.text: Forza Horizon 3 began development in 2014 after the release of Forza Horizon 2. Turn 10 Studios assisted with the game's development, as they did with other Forza Horizon games. Over the course of development, Playground Games tested different technological concepts for the game, while also trying to improve more features over the previous title. The Australian setting was chosen for its variety of regions, and a team was sent to Australia to conduct research for the game.

cards.heading: Praise for the map, criticism of progression
cards.text: Forza Horizon 3 was released in September 2016. At release, critics praised the map design, graphics, and amount of content, while most criticism was directed towards the monotony of the progression. The game won and was nominated for multiple awards and sold over 2.5 million copies in 2017. Downloadable content had also been released periodically, including two expansion packs. The game was followed by Forza Horizon 4, released in 2018.

main.title: Paper Mario: Color Splash
main.subtitle: An island losing its colour
main.summary: Paper Mario: Color Splash is a Wii U adventure set on Prism Island, where colour is being drained from the world. Mario joins Huey, a talking paint can, and searches for the missing Big Paint Stars. The paper-and-card setting makes that premise visible: damaged or empty-looking areas become invitations to restore something. Intelligent Systems builds the journey around exploration, puzzles and comic situations, using the craft materials of the world as part of its language rather than simply as a decorative treatment.

cards.heading: An island losing its colour
cards.text: Paper Mario: Color Splash is a Wii U adventure set on Prism Island, where colour is being drained from the world. Mario joins Huey, a talking paint can, and searches for the missing Big Paint Stars. The paper-and-card setting makes that premise visible: damaged or empty-looking areas become invitations to restore something. Intelligent Systems builds the journey around exploration, puzzles and comic situations, using the craft materials of the world as part of its language rather than simply as a decorative treatment.

cards.heading: Paint and a paper shortcut
cards.text: The hammer draws on a supply of red, blue and yellow paint. Filling an empty patch consumes the appropriate colour and can provide rewards; striking objects replenishes the supply. Hammer scraps increase how much Mario can carry. Another ability, Cutout, changes the route itself: tracing a dotted line on the GamePad touchscreen peels away part of the scenery and exposes a passage or secret. The island’s paper construction becomes a tool for exploration, giving Mario a way through places that initially look inaccessible.

cards.heading: Cards in the battle
cards.text: Combat uses cards, with the Wii U GamePad involved in choosing and painting attacks. The idea carries the game’s material theme into its turn-based encounters: an action is represented by something the player handles and prepares. Color Splash places particular emphasis on the pleasure of moving through its locations and finding their comic situations. That balance distinguishes this instalment within Paper Mario’s changing approach to role-playing. Its strongest identity comes from the consistency between what the island is made of and what Mario can do to it.

main.title: Monster Hunter Stories
main.subtitle: A Rider and their Monsties
main.summary: Monster Hunter Stories changes the hunt into a turn-based adventure about hatching, raising and travelling with monster companions.

cards.heading: A different relationship with monsters
cards.text: Monster Hunter Stories is Capcom?s 2016 Nintendo 3DS role-playing game, first released in Japan on October 8. A Rider hatches eggs, forms bonds with creatures called Monsties and explores alongside them. Turn-based battles replace the main series? real-time hunting. The Western release followed in September 2017.

cards.heading: Hatching and raising a team
cards.text: Players collect eggs and hatch Monsties to build a team. More than sixty creatures can become companions, each with uses in battle and exploration. Familiar monsters such as Rathalos and Velocidrome take on a different role as allies.

cards.heading: Turn-based combat and Kinship Skills
cards.text: During turn-based battles, the player selects actions and anticipates an opponent?s behaviour. Weapons and abilities draw on familiar series elements, while Kinship Skills let Rider and Monstie act together. Team choice and prediction shape the fight.

cards.heading: Companions help explore
cards.text: Monsties also provide ways to travel, including running and flying. Their abilities can open routes the Rider cannot reach alone. A demo accompanying the Western release let players carry opening progress and collected items into the full game.

main.title: Gears of War 4
main.subtitle: The Fenix Legacy
main.summary: Gears of War 4 is a 2016 third-person shooter game developed by The Coalition and published by Microsoft Studios for Windows and Xbox One.

cards.heading: A New Generation Faces the Swarm
cards.text: Gears of War 4 is a 2016 third-person shooter game developed by The Coalition and published by Microsoft Studios for Windows and Xbox One. It is the fourth main installment in the Gears of War series, and the first mainline entry not to be developed by Epic Games. Taking place 25 years after the events of Gears of War 3, the game's plot, which can be played in single or co-operative play, focuses on James Dominic "JD" Fenix, son of Marcus Fenix, as he and his allies take on the Swarm, a new threat related to the Locusts.

cards.heading: Reception and Continuation
cards.text: Upon release, the game received generally positive reviews, with critics praising the game's combat, visuals and set pieces, while criticism was directed towards the campaign and writing. A sequel, Gears 5, was released on September 10, 2019.

main.title: RIGS: Mechanized Combat League
main.subtitle: A pilot in the middle of the arena
main.summary: RIGS: Mechanized Combat League is Guerrilla Cambridge's virtual-reality arena shooter, released with PlayStation VR on 13 October 2016.

cards.heading: A pilot in the middle of the arena
cards.text: RIGS: Mechanized Combat League is Guerrilla Cambridge's virtual-reality arena shooter, released with PlayStation VR on 13 October 2016. Pilots compete in a futuristic professional sport using large armed machines called Rigs. Teams move through arenas inspired by real-world locations, combining combat with the objectives of a match. The headset places the player inside the machine, turning the height of a platform and the approach of another Rig into parts of the sporting space that must be read while fighting.

cards.heading: A machine chosen for its role
cards.text: Matches divide six competitors into two teams of three. Destroying an opposing Rig scores a takedown, while different competition types change the larger objective. Four classes provide the foundation for twenty-four machines, each with a weapon loadout and a particular ability. The selection matters to how a player contributes: a machine's mobility, weapons and special benefit shape the positions it can use effectively. The arena becomes a shared tactical problem, with teammates needing to combine their different machines rather than simply chase the nearest target.

cards.heading: Competitive sport at VR scale
cards.text: Five-minute matches split into two halves give the contest a clear sporting frame. Barnabas and Arnold composed the music, and Guerrilla's Decima technology supported the production. RIGS joined the original headset's launch lineup as an experiment in competitive virtual-reality action. Its online service closed in August 2022, an important boundary in the history of a game built partly around team competition. The original design remains an example of placing a familiar arena match inside a vehicle whose size and cockpit are experienced through a headset.

main.title: Until Dawn: Rush of Blood
main.subtitle: A haunted ride that keeps moving
main.summary: Until Dawn: Rush of Blood is Supermassive Games' virtual-reality rail shooter, released for PlayStation VR on 13 October 2016.

cards.heading: A haunted ride that keeps moving
cards.text: Until Dawn: Rush of Blood is Supermassive Games' virtual-reality rail shooter, released for PlayStation VR on 13 October 2016. A roller-coaster carriage carries the player through a horror-themed carnival, with enemies and targets appearing along the route. The ride controls the journey while the player aims and reacts to the threats around it. The premise makes the headset's enclosed viewpoint part of the attraction: the track continues forward, and the next disturbing scene can emerge beside the carriage as readily as ahead.

cards.heading: Shoot while the track decides the route
cards.text: Seven roller-coaster stages combine moving scenery with shooting encounters. The player begins with handguns and finds other weapons along the way. Each section arranges targets and live enemies around the changing position of the cart, making looking and aiming inseparable from the ride's progress. A bend or sudden descent changes the angle of the next encounter without asking the player to steer. The game's limited route gives it control over timing, while the surrounding virtual space leaves the player responsible for noticing where danger has appeared.

cards.heading: Familiar horror in another form
cards.text: The game draws locations and figures from Until Dawn into a more theatrical carnival structure. Hallucinations and shifting tracks let the familiar horror material transform as the ride progresses, connecting the separate shooting galleries through an increasingly unstable journey. Jason Graves composed the music. Released alongside the first PlayStation VR headset, Rush of Blood uses a recognizable amusement-park form to introduce its movement: the player is seated in a carriage, but the view around that seat supplies the scale and immediacy of the attraction.
